/-!
# The damping majorant from exact vanishing of the complement jets

`AbeDampingPacketData.majorant` bounds the *packet jets* of the complement Poincaré terms, not the
terms themselves.  So a seed whose complement translates vanish to the packet order satisfies it
exactly, with constant `0`: the bound is then `0 ≤ 0`, with no `B`-dependence at all.

This is worth isolating, because it changes the shape of the analytic obligation.  What has to be
constructed is not a damping multiplier — a `ΓH`-invariant entire multiplier is a holomorphic
function on the toroidal quotient `ℂ^d/ΓH`, hence constant when that quotient is toroidal, and
otherwise a character whose modulus is *linear* in the complement index and therefore grows on half
of the complement lattice — but a family of lower-automorphic seeds with the prescribed packet jets
whose complement translates vanish there.

* `abeDampingMajorant_of_jet_vanishing` — the majorant from vanishing;
* `AbeDampingPacketData.ofVanishing` — the packet datum from vanishing.
-/

open Filter Function Set Topology

theorem abeDampingMajorant_of_jet_vanishing {d c : ℕ} {Γ : AddSubgroup (Fin d → ℂ)}

      multiIndexJetEvalCLM (w i.1) i.2.1
          (poincareTermEntire upper (seed B j) (complementEmbedding comp comp_mem z)) = 0) :
    ∃ (A : Fin c → ℕ) (sigma : Fin c → ℝ) (r : ℕ) (delta C : ℝ),

      ∀ B : ℝ, 0 ≤ B → ∀ (z : Fin c → ℤ) (i j : FiniteJetPacketIndex d I m), z ≠ 0 →

  seed := seed

At one subgroup-rank extension, a lower-factor section must retain prescribed mixed jets on the
original packet and vanish through the same orders at finitely many nonzero complement translates.
This is not a new analytic interpolation problem: those points form one larger packet for the lower

damping argument.

This theorem deliberately supplies no global normalized-growth bound.  That quantitative bound is
the remaining analytic core of the all-order Abe extension, and cannot follow from surjectivity of

-/

    (t : T → Fin c → ℤ) (ht : Function.Injective t)
    (s₀ : T) (hs₀ : t s₀ = 0)
    (hdistinct : PairwiseDistinctModulo Γ w)
    (lowerColumn : FiniteJetPacketIndex d I m → lower.forms) :
    ∃ seed : FiniteJetPacketIndex d I m → lower.forms,
      (∀ j (i : FiniteJetPacketIndex d I m),
        multiIndexJetEvalCLM (w i.1) i.2.1 (seed j).1 =
          multiIndexJetEvalCLM (w i.1) i.2.1 (lowerColumn j).1) ∧
      (∀ j (i : I) s (a : FiniteJetMultiIndex d (m i)), s ≠ s₀ →
        multiIndexJetEvalCLM (w i + comp (t s)) a.1 (seed j).1 = 0) := by
  classical

  let m' : I × T → ℕ := fun p => m p.1

      lower.jetPacketLinearMap w' m' (seed j) = fun q =>
        if q.1.2 = s₀ then
          multiIndexJetEvalCLM (w q.1.1) q.2.1 (lowerColumn j).1
        else 0 :=
    Classical.choose_spec (hsurj fun q =>
      if q.1.2 = s₀ then
        multiIndexJetEvalCLM (w q.1.1) q.2.1 (lowerColumn j).1
      else 0)
  refine ⟨seed, ?_, ?_⟩

    let q : FiniteJetPacketIndex d (I × T) m' := ⟨(i, s), a⟩

    simpa [AutomorphicFactor.jetPacketLinearMap_apply, w', m', q, hs] using h

end

/-!
# Finite interpolation with vanishing at the translates

Prescribing jets at a packet *and* zero jets at finitely many translates of it is a single
interpolation problem on the enlarged packet, so the corpus's packet surjectivity solves it
outright: one multivariable polynomial realises every mixed partial below the prescribed order at
finitely many distinct points.

The points of the enlarged packet are distinct because the base points are distinct modulo the full
lattice and the complement meets the lower lattice only at zero — which is
`pairwiseDistinctModulo_enlargedPacketPoints`, stated there for the quotient and used here through
plain injectivity.

* `exists_mvPolynomial_packet_and_vanishing`.
-/

theorem exists_mvPolynomial_packet_and_vanishing {d c : ℕ} {I T : Type*} [Finite I] [Finite T]
    (w : I → Fin d → ℂ) (comp : (Fin c → ℤ) →+ (Fin d → ℂ)) (t : T → (Fin c → ℤ))
    (hinj : Function.Injective (enlargedPacketPoints w comp t))
    (m : I → ℕ) (jet : I → (Fin d →₀ ℕ) → ℂ) (s₀ : T) (hs₀ : t s₀ = 0) :
    ∃ P : MvPolynomial (Fin d) ℂ,
      (∀ i (a : Fin d →₀ ℕ), Finsupp.degree a < m i →
        multiIndexJetEvalCLM (w i) a (mvPolynomialMultivariateEntire P) = jet i a) ∧
      (∀ i (s : T), s ≠ s₀ → ∀ a : Fin d →₀ ℕ, Finsupp.degree a < m i →
        multiIndexJetEvalCLM (w i + comp (t s)) a (mvPolynomialMultivariateEntire P) = 0) := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨P, hP⟩ := exists_mvPolynomial_multiIndexJetEvalCLM_eq_arbitrary
    (enlargedPacketPoints w comp t) hinj (fun p => m p.1)
    (fun p a => if p.2 = s₀ then jet p.1 a else 0)
  refine ⟨P, fun i a ha => ?_, fun i s hs a ha => ?_⟩
  · have h := hP (i, s₀) a ha
    have hif : (if ((i, s₀) : I × T).2 = s₀ then jet ((i, s₀) : I × T).1 a else 0) = jet i a :=

    rw [hif] at h

      rw [enlargedPacketPoints_apply, hs₀, map_zero, add_zero]
    rwa [hpt] at h
  · have h := hP (i, s) a ha

/-!
# Polarized incidence and the capacity-phase separation

On a finite signed multigraph whose every edge runs from a positive to a negative vertex, the
diagonal Möbius polarization `S_ε` turns the signless endpoint incidence `B⁺` into the ordinary
oriented boundary `∂`.  Polarization is diagonal with unimodular entries, so it changes no vertex
label, no support, no absolute coordinate norm, and nothing at all on edges — in particular no edge
capacity and no absolute edge-work functional.

Consequently the capacity residual `r = w - B⁺q` obeys a polarized discrete Stokes law
`S_ε w = ∂q + S_ε r`, whose piAugmentation and cut-pairing forms say that the polarized source charge
is a signed cut flux plus an unmatched residual.  On a connected graph the degree-zero quotient is
one dimensional and the polarized class is exactly the signed total capacity.

The finite ordered-prime path realizes the same boundary type through the exact Abel decomposition
`z_N = ∂q_N + b_N`.  But the two capacity geometries are not the same: the Abel prefix primitive
`T_{n+1}` is unbounded relative to the natural local edge capacity `t_{n+1}`, and the associated
log-gap work diverges.  So a common polarized degree-zero boundary type does not imply a common
capacity-filtered boundary phase.
-/

# The canonical bilinear form on a finite root pairing

Given a finite root pairing, we define a canonical map from weight space to coweight space, and the
corresponding bilinear form. This form is symmetric and Weyl-invariant, and if the base ring is
linearly ordered, then the form is root-positive, positive-semidefinite on the weight space, and
positive-definite on the span of roots.
From these facts, it is easy to show that Coxeter weights in a finite root pairing are bounded
above by 4. Thus, the pairings of roots and coroots in a crystallographic root pairing are
restricted to a small finite set of possibilities.
Another application is to the faithfulness of the Weyl group action on roots, and finiteness of the
Weyl group.

## Main definitions:
* `RootPairing.Polarization`: A distinguished linear map from the weight space to the coweight
  space.
* `RootPairing.RootForm` : The bilinear form on weight space corresponding to `Polarization`.

## Main results:
* `RootPairing.rootForm_self_sum_of_squares` : The inner product of any
  weight vector is a sum of squares.
* `RootPairing.rootForm_reflection_reflection_apply` : `RootForm` is invariant with respect
  to reflections.
* `RootPairing.rootForm_self_smul_coroot`: The inner product of a root with itself
  times the corresponding coroot is equal to two times Polarization applied to the root.
* `RootPairing.exists_ge_zero_eq_rootForm`: `RootForm` is positive semidefinite.

## References:
* [N. Bourbaki, *Lie groups and Lie algebras. Chapters 4--6*][bourbaki1968]
* [M. Demazure, *SGA III, Exposé XXI, Données Radicielles*][demazure1970]

/-!
# Matrix-valued event-square polarization

For a finite complex matrix `X`, its event square is the positive Gram record `Xᴴ X`.
Evaluating this one quadratic map on the four superpositions `X ± Y` and `X ± iY`
recovers the complete ordered cross-Gram matrix `Xᴴ Y`.

This is the standard complex polarization identity with a matrix-valued codomain. It does not
identify amplitudes with physical events, Gram matrices with spacetime, or their symmetries with
forces.
-/

open Matrix
open scoped Matrix

noncomputable section

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

variable {m n : Type*} [Fintype m]

/-- Positive quadratic Gram record associated with a finite complex matrix. -/
def eventSquare (X : Matrix m n ℂ) : Matrix n n ℂ :=
  Xᴴ * X

/-- Ordered sesquilinear cross-Gram record of two finite complex matrices. -/
def eventCrossGram (X Y : Matrix m n ℂ) : Matrix n n ℂ :=
  Xᴴ * Y

/-- The real-polarization difference recovers twice the Hermitian cross term. -/
theorem eventSquare_add_sub_polarization (X Y : Matrix m n ℂ) :
    eventSquare (X + Y) - eventSquare (X - Y) =
      (2 : ℂ) • (eventCrossGram X Y + eventCrossGram Y X) := by
  rw [two_smul ℂ]
  ext i j
  simp only [eventSquare, eventCrossGram, Matrix.sub_apply, Matrix.add_apply,
    Matrix.mul_apply, Matrix.conjTranspose_apply]
  rw [← Finset.sum_sub_distrib, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib,
    ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro x _
  have hstarAdd :
      star (X x i + Y x i) = star (X x i) + star (Y x i) :=
    (starAddEquiv : ℂ ≃+ ℂ).map_add _ _
  rw [hstarAdd, star_sub]
  ring

/-- The imaginary-polarization difference recovers twice `i` times the skew cross term. -/
theorem eventSquare_i_add_sub_polarization (X Y : Matrix m n ℂ) :
    eventSquare (X + Complex.I • Y) -
        eventSquare (X - Complex.I • Y) =
      (2 * Complex.I) • (eventCrossGram X Y - eventCrossGram Y X) := by
  rw [eventSquare_add_sub_polarization]
  simp [eventCrossGram, Matrix.conjTranspose_smul, Matrix.mul_smul,
    Matrix.smul_mul, sub_eq_add_neg, smul_smul]

/-- Full matrix-valued complex polarization: four event-square evaluations recover `Xᴴ Y`. -/
theorem eventCrossGram_eq_eventSquare_polarization (X Y : Matrix m n ℂ) :
    eventCrossGram X Y =
      (1 / 4 : ℂ) •
        ((eventSquare (X + Y) - eventSquare (X - Y)) -
          Complex.I •
            (eventSquare (X + Complex.I • Y) -
              eventSquare (X - Complex.I • Y))) := by
  rw [eventSquare_add_sub_polarization,
    eventSquare_i_add_sub_polarization]
  simp [smul_smul, sub_eq_add_neg]
  ring_nf
  rw [Complex.I_sq]
  ext i j
  simp
  ring
